sanskrit: sa tasya madhye bhavanasya vānaro latāgṛhāṃś citragṛhān niśāgṛhān jagāma sītāṃ prati darśanotsuko na caiva tāṃ paśyati cārudarśanām
english: That monkey moved through the inner chambers of his palace — the bower-houses, the painted halls, the night-chambers — eager to behold Sītā, yet nowhere did he see her, she of lovely form.

sanskrit: sa cintayām āsa tato mahākapiḥ priyām apaśyan raghunandanasya tām dhruvaṃ nu sītā mriyate yathā na me vicinvato darśanam eti maithilī
english: Then that great monkey, not finding her who is dear to the son of Raghu, reflected: "Surely Sītā must be dead, since Maithilī does not come within my sight however thoroughly I search."

sanskrit: sā rākṣasānāṃ pravareṇa bālā svaśīlasaṃrakṣaṇa tat parā satī anena nūnaṃ pratiduṣṭakarmaṇā hatā bhaved āryapathe pare sthitā
english: "That young woman, devoted entirely to guarding her own virtue, a faithful wife, standing firm on the noble path — she must surely have been slain by this wicked evildoer."

sanskrit: virūparūpā vikṛtā vivarcaso mahānanā dīrghavirūpadarśanāḥ samīkṣya sā rākṣasarājayoṣito bhayād vinaṣṭā janakeśvarātmajā
english: "Having looked upon the wives of the king of rākṣasas — misshapen, deformed, sallow, great-mouthed, tall and hideous in appearance — the daughter of the lord of Janaka may have perished from sheer terror."

sanskrit: sītām adṛṣṭvā hy anavāpya pauruṣaṃ vihṛtya kālaṃ saha vānaraiś ciram na me 'sti sugrīvasamīpagā gatiḥ sutīkṣṇadaṇḍo balavāṃś ca vānaraḥ
english: "Having failed to find Sītā and having accomplished no heroic deed, after spending so long a time with the monkeys, there is no way for me to return to Sugrīva's presence — he is powerful and swift in punishment."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭam antaḥpuraṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇayoṣitaḥ na sītā dṛśyate sādhvī vṛthā jāto mama śramaḥ
english: "The entire inner palace has been searched; I have seen Rāvaṇa's women; yet the virtuous Sītā is nowhere to be found. My effort has been in vain."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu māṃ vānarāḥ sarve gataṃ vakṣyanti saṃgatāḥ gatvā tatra tvayā vīra kiṃ kṛtaṃ tad vadasva naḥ
english: "What will all the assembled monkeys say to me when I return? They will ask: 'Tell us, hero, what did you accomplish when you went there?'"

sanskrit: adṛṣṭvā kiṃ pravakṣyāmi tām ahaṃ janakātmajām dhruvaṃ prāyam upeṣyanti kālasya vyativartane
english: "What shall I say, not having found the daughter of Janaka? When time runs out, they will surely undertake a fast unto death."

sanskrit: kiṃ vā vakṣyati vṛddhaś ca jāmbavān aṅgadaś ca saḥ gataṃ pāraṃ samudrasya vānarāś ca samāgatāḥ
english: "What will old Jāmbavān say, and Aṅgada, and the assembled monkeys who have crossed to the far shore of the ocean?"

sanskrit: anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlam anirvedaḥ paraṃ sukham bhūyas tāvad viceṣyāmi na yatra vicayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Perseverance is the root of prosperity; perseverance is the highest happiness. I shall search again those places not yet searched."

sanskrit: anirvedo hi satataṃ sarvārtheṣu pravartakaḥ karoti saphalaṃ jantoḥ karma yac ca karoti saḥ
english: "For perseverance ever drives a being forward in all endeavors and renders fruitful whatever action that being undertakes."

sanskrit: tasmād anirveda kṛtaṃ yatnaṃ ceṣṭe 'ham uttamam adṛṣṭāṃś ca viceṣyāmi deśān rāvaṇapālitān
english: "Therefore I shall exert the best effort born of perseverance, and search those quarters of Rāvaṇa's realm not yet examined."

sanskrit: āpānaśālāvicitās tathā puṣpagṛhāṇi ca citraśālāś ca vicitā bhūyaḥ krīḍāgṛhāṇi ca
english: "The drinking halls have been searched, and the flower-houses too; the picture galleries have been examined as well as the pleasure-chambers."

sanskrit: niṣkuṭāntararathyāś ca vimānāni ca sarvaśaḥ iti saṃcintya bhūyo 'pi vicetum upacakrame
english: "The inner lanes of the groves, the aerial palaces — all have been scrutinized." Having thus reflected, he set about searching again.

sanskrit: bhūmīgṛhāṃś caityagṛhān gṛhātigṛhakān api utpatan nipataṃś cāpi tiṣṭhan gacchan punaḥ kva cit
english: Underground chambers, shrines, dwellings and smaller outbuildings — leaping up and dropping down, standing still and moving on, turning in every direction,

sanskrit: apāvṛṇvaṃś ca dvārāṇi kapāṭāny avaghaṭṭayan praviśan niṣpataṃś cāpi prapatann utpatann api sarvam apy avakāśaṃ sa vicacāra mahākapiḥ
english: — throwing open doors, pushing at panels, entering and issuing forth, diving down and springing up — that great monkey explored every single space.

sanskrit: caturaṅgulamātro 'pi nāvakāśaḥ sa vidyate rāvaṇāntaḥpure tasmin yaṃ kapir na jagāma saḥ
english: There was not even a four-finger-wide space in that inner palace of Rāvaṇa which the monkey did not enter.

sanskrit: prākārāntararathyāś ca vedikaś caityasaṃśrayāḥ śvabhrāś ca puṣkariṇyaś ca sarvaṃ tenāvalokitam
english: The lanes within the ramparts, the altars and their shrines, the chasms and the lotus pools — all were surveyed by him.

sanskrit: rākṣasyo vividhākārā virūpā vikṛtās tathā dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sā janakātmajā
english: Rākṣasī women of every shape, misshapen and deformed, were seen by Hanūmat there — but not that daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: rūpeṇāpratimā loke varā vidyādhara striyaḥ dṛṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu rāghavanandinī
english: Vidyādhara women of unrivalled beauty in the world were seen by Hanūmat there — but not she who is the beloved of Rāghava.

sanskrit: nāgakanyā varārohāḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sītā sumadhyamā
english: Nāga maidens of noble bearing, their faces like the full moon, were seen by Hanūmat there — but not slender-waisted Sītā.

sanskrit: pramathya rākṣasendreṇa nāgakanyā balād dhṛtāḥ dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na sā janakanandinī
english: Nāga maidens seized by force by the lord of rākṣasas and held in subjugation were seen by Hanūmat there — but not that daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: so 'paśyaṃs tāṃ mahābāhuḥ paśyaṃś cānyā varastriyaḥ viṣasāda mahābāhur hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Not finding her, yet seeing all those other noble women — the mighty-armed Hanūmat, son of the Wind, fell into despondency.

sanskrit: udyogaṃ vānarendrāṇaṃ plavanaṃ sāgarasya ca vyarthaṃ vīkṣyānilasutaś cintāṃ punar upāgamat
english: Seeing the great effort of the monkey chiefs and the crossing of the ocean rendered fruitless, the son of the Wind fell once more into anxious thought.

sanskrit: avatīrya vimānāc ca hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ cintām upajagāmātha śokopahatacetanaḥ
english: Hanūmat, son of the Wind, descended from the aerial palace and fell into reflection, his mind stricken with grief.

sanskrit: vimānāt tu susaṃkramya prākāraṃ hariyūthapaḥ hanūmān vegavān āsīd yathā vidyudghanāntare
english: Crossing easily from the aerial palace to the rampart, Hanūmat, swift lord of the monkey host, was like lightning lodged within a cloud.

sanskrit: saṃparikramya hanumān rāvaṇasya niveśanān adṛṣṭvā jānakīṃ sītām abravīd vacanaṃ kapiḥ
english: Having roamed all about Rāvaṇa's dwelling and not found Jānakī Sītā, the monkey spoke these words:

sanskrit: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ loḍitā laṅkā rāmasya caratā priyam na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṃ sītāṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanām
english: "Laṅkā has been searched most thoroughly in service of Rāma, yet I do not see Vaidehī Sītā, she who is beautiful in every limb."

sanskrit: palvalāni taṭākāni sarāṃsi saritas tathā nadyo 'nūpavanāntāś ca durgāś ca dharaṇīdharāḥ loḍitā vasudhā sarvā na ca paśyāmi jānakīm
english: "Pools, lakes, ponds and rivers, streams with marshy groves along their banks, mountain fastnesses — the whole earth has been searched, yet I do not see Jānakī."

sanskrit: iha saṃpātinā sītā rāvaṇasya niveśane ākhyātā gṛdhrarājena na ca paśyāmi tām aham
english: "Here in Rāvaṇa's dwelling Sītā was pointed out by Saṃpāti, king of vultures, yet I do not find her."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu sītātha vaidehī maithilī janakātmajā upatiṣṭheta vivaśā rāvaṇaṃ duṣṭacāriṇam
english: "Would Sītā — Vaidehī, Maithilī, daughter of Janaka — ever willingly submit to Rāvaṇa, that wicked-natured one?"

sanskrit: kṣipram utpatato manye sītām ādāya rakṣasaḥ bibhyato rāmabāṇānām antarā patitā bhavet
english: "I think the rākṣasa, fleeing swiftly in terror of Rāma's arrows while carrying Sītā, may have let her fall midway."

sanskrit: atha vā hriyamāṇāyāḥ pathi siddhaniṣevite manye patitam āryāyā hṛdayaṃ prekṣya sāgaram
english: "Or else, while being carried along the path frequented by siddhas, the noble lady's heart may have failed upon beholding the ocean below."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasyoruvegena bhujābhyāṃ pīḍitena ca tayā manye viśālākṣyā tyaktaṃ jīvitam āryayā
english: "Crushed by the great speed of Rāvaṇa and pressed by his arms, I think that wide-eyed noble lady may have surrendered her life."

sanskrit: upary upari vā nūnaṃ sāgaraṃ kramatas tadā viveṣṭamānā patitā samudre janakātmajā
english: "Or perhaps, as Rāvaṇa traversed higher and higher over the ocean, the daughter of Janaka, writhing in his grasp, fell into the sea."

sanskrit: āho kṣudreṇa cānena rakṣantī śīlam ātmanaḥ abandhur bhakṣitā sītā rāvaṇena tapasvinī
english: "Or perhaps, while guarding her own chastity from this wretched creature, helpless Sītā, that ascetic woman, was devoured by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: atha vā rākṣasendrasya patnībhir asitekṣaṇā aduṣṭā duṣṭabhāvābhir bhakṣitā sā bhaviṣyati
english: "Or she of dark eyes, though herself guiltless, may have been devoured by the wives of the rākṣasa king, those women of evil intent."

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇacandrapratimaṃ padmapatranibhekṣaṇam rāmasya dhyāyatī vaktraṃ pañcatvaṃ kṛpaṇā gatā
english: "Meditating on Rāma's face — like the full moon, with eyes resembling lotus petals — that wretched woman may have perished."

sanskrit: hā rāma lakṣmaṇety eva hāyodhyeti ca maithilī vilapya bahu vaidehī nyastadehā bhaviṣyati
english: "Crying out again and again 'Oh Rāma! Oh Lakṣmaṇa!' and 'Oh Ayodhyā!', Maithilī Vaidehī may have laid down her body."

sanskrit: atha vā nihitā manye rāvaṇasya niveśane nūnaṃ lālapyate mandaṃ pañjarastheva śārikā
english: "Or perhaps she is confined somewhere in Rāvaṇa's dwelling, piteously murmuring like a myna bird in a cage."

sanskrit: janakasya kule jātā rāmapatnī sumadhyamā katham utpalapatrākṣī rāvaṇasya vaśaṃ vrajet
english: "Born in Janaka's lineage, Rāma's wife, slender-waisted, with eyes like lotus petals — how could she ever submit to Rāvaṇa's will?"

sanskrit: vinaṣṭā vā pranaṣṭā vā mṛtā vā janakātmajā rāmasya priyabhāryasya na nivedayituṃ kṣamam
english: "Whether the daughter of Janaka is destroyed, disappeared, or dead — it is not proper to report such news to Rāma, who loved her as his wife."

sanskrit: nivedyamāne doṣaḥ syād doṣaḥ syād anivedane kathaṃ nu khalu kartavyaṃ viṣamaṃ pratibhāti me
english: "There would be harm in telling him; there would be harm in not telling him. What truly must be done seems difficult to discern."

sanskrit: asminn evaṃgate karye prāptakālaṃ kṣamaṃ ca kim bhaved iti matiṃ bhūyo hanumān pravicārayan
english: "With matters thus arrived at this pass, what would be timely and proper?" Hanūmān deliberated thus at length.

sanskrit: yadi sītām adṛṣṭvāhaṃ vānarendrapurīm itaḥ gamiṣyāmi tataḥ ko me puruṣārtho bhaviṣyati
english: "If I return from here to the city of the monkey king without having found Sītā, what human purpose will have been achieved by me?"

sanskrit: mamedaṃ laṅghanaṃ vyarthaṃ sāgarasya bhaviṣyati praveśaś civa laṅkāyā rākṣasānāṃ ca darśanam
english: "This crossing of the ocean on my part will have been fruitless, as will my entry into Laṅkā and my seeing the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: kiṃ vā vakṣyati sugrīvo harayo va samāgatāḥ kiṣkindhāṃ samanuprāptau tau vā daśarathātmajau
english: "What will Sugrīva say, or the assembled monkeys, or those two sons of Daśaratha, when I reach Kiṣkindhā?"

sanskrit: gatvā tu yadi kākutsthaṃ vakṣyāmi param apriyam na dṛṣṭeti mayā sītā tatas tyakṣyanti jīvitam
english: "If I go and report to Kākutstha the most grievous news — that Sītā has not been found by me — he will abandon his life."

sanskrit: paruṣaṃ dāruṇaṃ krūraṃ tīkṣṇam indriyatāpanam sītānimittaṃ durvākyaṃ śrutvā sa na bhaviṣyati
english: "Upon hearing those harsh, terrible, cruel, keen, sense-tormenting, ill words occasioned by Sītā, he will cease to exist."

sanskrit: taṃ tu kṛcchragataṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcatvagatamānasaṃ bhṛśānurakto medhāvī na bhaviṣyati lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "Seeing him plunged in anguish, his heart dissolved in death, Lakṣmaṇa — devoted to him most deeply, though wise — will not survive."

sanskrit: vinaṣṭau bhrātarau śrutvā bharato 'pi mariṣyati bharataṃ ca mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatrughno na bhaviṣyati
english: "Upon hearing that both brothers are dead, Bharata too will die; and seeing Bharata dead, Śatrughna will not survive."

sanskrit: putrān mṛtān samīkṣyātha na bhaviṣyanti mātaraḥ kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Looking upon their dead sons, the mothers — Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī — will not survive either; of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: kṛtajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ rāmaṃ tathā gataṃ dṛṣṭvā tatas tyakṣyanti jīvitam
english: "Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, grateful and true to his word, will abandon his life upon seeing Rāma thus departed."

sanskrit: durmanā vyathitā dīnā nirānandā tapasvinī pīḍitā bhartṛśokena rumā tyakṣyati jīvitam
english: "Dejected, distressed, wretched, joyless, tormented by grief for her husband, Rumā will relinquish her life."

sanskrit: vālijena tu duḥkhena pīḍitā śokakarśitā pañcatvagamane rājñas tārāpi na bhaviṣyati
english: "Afflicted by the sorrow caused by Vālin's son and worn by grief, Tārā too will not survive the king's death."

sanskrit: mātāpitror vināśena sugrīva vyasanena ca kumāro 'py aṅgadaḥ kasmād dhārayiṣyati jīvitam
english: "With the loss of both his parents and Sugrīva's calamity upon him, how will prince Aṅgada maintain his life?"

sanskrit: bhartṛjena tu śokena abhibhūtā vanaukasaḥ śirāṃsy abhihaniṣyanti talair muṣṭibhir eva ca
english: "Overwhelmed by grief arising from their master's death, the forest-dwellers will beat their heads with palms and fists."

sanskrit: sāntvenānupradānena mānena ca yaśasvinī lālitāḥ kapirājena prāṇāṃs tyakṣyanti vānarāḥ
english: "The monkeys, who were cherished by the glorious monkey king with conciliation, gifts and honor, will cast away their lives."

sanskrit: na vaneṣu na śaileṣu na nirodheṣu vā punaḥ krīḍām anubhaviṣyanti sametya kapikuñjarāḥ
english: "The lordly elephants among monkeys, gathered together, will sport no more in forests, on mountains, nor in groves."

sanskrit: saputradārāḥ sāmātyā bhartṛvyasanapīḍitāḥ śailāgrebhyaḥ patiṣyanti sametya viṣameṣu ca
english: "With their sons and wives and ministers, tormented by the calamity that befell their master, they will hurl themselves from mountain peaks and precipices."

sanskrit: viṣam udbandhanaṃ vāpi praveśaṃ jvalanasya vā upavāsam atho śastraṃ pracariṣyanti vānarāḥ
english: "The monkeys will resort to poison, hanging, entering fire, starvation, or the sword."

sanskrit: ghoram ārodanaṃ manye gate mayi bhaviṣyati ikṣvākukulanāśaś ca nāśaś caiva vanaukasām
english: "I think, if I depart without success, there will be terrible weeping, and the ruin of the Ikṣvāku lineage together with the destruction of the forest-dwellers."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ naiva gamiṣyāmi kiṣkindhāṃ nagarīm itaḥ na hi śakṣyāmy ahaṃ draṣṭuṃ sugrīvaṃ maithilīṃ vinā
english: "Therefore I shall not return from here to the city of Kiṣkindhā, for I cannot bear to look upon Sugrīva without Maithilī."

sanskrit: mayy agacchati cehasthe dharmātmānau mahārathau āśayā tau dhariṣyete vanarāś ca manasvinaḥ
english: "If I remain here without returning, those two great warriors of righteous soul, and the spirited monkeys, will sustain themselves on hope."

sanskrit: hastādāno mukhādāno niyato vṛkṣamūlikaḥ vānaprastho bhaviṣyāmi adṛṣṭvā janakātmajām
english: "Taking food only by hand or by mouth, restrained, dwelling at the root of a tree, I shall become a forest ascetic without having found the daughter of Janaka."

sanskrit: sāgarānūpaje deśe bahumūlaphalodake citāṃ kṛtvā pravekṣyāmi samiddham araṇīsutam
english: "In a place beside the ocean, rich in roots and fruit, I shall build a funeral pyre and enter the fire kindled from the araṇī wood."

sanskrit: upaviṣṭasya vā samyag liṅginaṃ sādhayiṣyataḥ śarīraṃ bhakṣayiṣyanti vāyasāḥ śvāpadāni ca
english: "Or, sitting still and properly observing the rites of one who bears the marks of renunciation, crows and beasts of prey will devour my body."

sanskrit: idam apy ṛṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ niryāṇam iti me matiḥ samyag āpaḥ pravekṣyāmi na cet paśyāmi jānakīm
english: "This too is a departure approved by the seers, I believe: I shall properly enter the waters, if I do not find Jānakī."

sanskrit: sujātamūlā subhagā kīrtimālāyaśasvinī prabhagnā cirarātrīyaṃ mama sītām apaśyataḥ
english: "Well-rooted, fortunate, wreathed in glory and fame — this long-standing honor of mine is now shattered, I who have not found Sītā."

sanskrit: tāpaso vā bhaviṣyāmi niyato vṛkṣamūlikaḥ netaḥ pratigamiṣyāmi tām adṛṣṭvāsitekṣaṇām
english: "I shall become an ascetic, restrained, dwelling at the root of a tree — I shall not return from here without finding her of dark eyes."

sanskrit: yadītaḥ pratigacchāmi sītām anadhigamya tām aṅgadaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair vānarair na bhaviṣyati
english: "If I return from here without obtaining Sītā, Aṅgada together with all the monkeys will not survive."

sanskrit: vināśe bahavo doṣā jīvan prāpnoti bhadrakam tasmāt prāṇān dhariṣyāmi dhruvo jīvati saṃgamaḥ
english: "In dying there are many faults; in living one attains what is good. Therefore I shall preserve my life — while one lives, reunion is certain."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ duḥkhaṃ manasā dhārayan muhuḥ nādhyagacchat tadā pāraṃ śokasya kapikuñjaraḥ
english: "Thus repeatedly bearing many forms of anguish in his mind, that lordly elephant among monkeys could find no end to his grief."

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ vā vadhiṣyāmi daśagrīvaṃ mahābalam kāmam astu hṛtā sītā pratyācīrṇaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Or I shall slay Rāvaṇa, the mighty ten-necked one; let Sītā have been carried off — it shall be requited."

sanskrit: atha vā vainaṃ samutkṣipya upary upari sāgaram rāmāyopahariṣyāmi paśuṃ paśupater iva
english: "Or else I shall seize him and carry him above the ocean to Rāma as a sacrificial beast to the lord of sacrificial beasts."

sanskrit: iti cintā samāpannaḥ sītām anadhigamya tām dhyānaśokā parītātmā cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Thus the monkey, having entered upon these deliberations, not having found Sītā, his soul overwhelmed by meditative grief, continued to reflect.

sanskrit: yāvat sītāṃ na paśyāmi rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm tāvad etāṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ vicinomi punaḥ punaḥ
english: "As long as I do not find Sītā, the glorious wife of Rāma, I shall search this city of Laṅkā again and again."

sanskrit: saṃpāti vacanāc cāpi rāmaṃ yady ānayāmy aham apaśyan rāghavo bhāryāṃ nirdahet sarvavānarān
english: "And if I bring Rāma here on account of Saṃpāti's word, Rāghava, not finding his wife, would burn all the monkeys."

sanskrit: ihaiva niyatāhāro vatsyāmi niyatendriyaḥ na matkṛte vinaśyeyuḥ sarve te naravānarāḥ
english: "I shall remain right here with measured food and restrained senses; let not all those men and monkeys perish on my account."

sanskrit: aśokavanikā cāpi mahatīyaṃ mahādrumā imām abhigamiṣyāmi na hīyaṃ vicitā mayā
english: "There is also this great Aśoka grove with its mighty trees — I shall approach it, for it has not been searched by me."

sanskrit: vasūn rudrāṃs tathādityān aśvinau maruto 'pi ca namaskṛtvā gamiṣyāmi rakṣasāṃ śokavardhanaḥ
english: "Paying homage to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Aśvins and the Maruts, I shall go there as one who augments the grief of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: jitvā tu rākṣasān devīm ikṣvākukulanandinīm saṃpradāsyāmi rāmāyā yathāsiddhiṃ tapasvine
english: "Having conquered the rākṣasas, I shall deliver the queen, delight of the Ikṣvāku lineage, to Rāma the ascetic, proportionate to success."

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā cintāvigrathitendriyaḥ udatiṣṭhan mahābāhur hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Having reflected for a moment, his senses knotted with care, the mighty-armed Hanūmān, son of the Wind, arose.

sanskrit: namo 'stu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya devyai ca tasyai janakātmajāyai namo 'stu rudrendrayamānilebhyo namo 'stu candrārkamarudgaṇebhyaḥ
english: "Homage to Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa; homage to that goddess, the daughter of Janaka; homage to Rudra, Indra, Yama and the Wind; homage to the Moon, the Sun and the hosts of Maruts."

sanskrit: sa tebhyas tu namaskṛtvā sugrīvāya ca mārutiḥ diśaḥ sarvāḥ samālokya aśokavanikāṃ prati
english: Having paid those homages and to Sugrīva as well, the son of the Wind surveyed all the directions and turned toward the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: sa gatvā manasā pūrvam aśokavanikāṃ śubhām uttaraṃ cintayām āsa vānaro mārutātmajaḥ
english: Going first in his mind to the lovely Aśoka grove, the monkey, son of the Wind, then reflected further:

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ tu rakṣobahulā bhaviṣyati vanākulā aśokavanikā cintyā sarvasaṃskārasaṃskṛtā
english: "Surely the Aśoka grove, well-tended with every cultivation, will be full of rākṣasas and crowded with forest creatures."

sanskrit: rakṣiṇaś cātra vihitā nūnaṃ rakṣanti pādapān bhagavān api sarvātmā nātikṣobhaṃ pravāyati
english: "Guards are surely appointed there to protect the trees; even the omnipresent lord of all does not blow there with excessive disturbance."

sanskrit: saṃkṣipto 'yaṃ mayātmā ca rāmārthe rāvaṇasya ca siddhiṃ me saṃvidhāsyanti devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tv iha
english: "This form of mine has been contracted for Rāma's sake and for Rāvaṇa's undoing; the gods together with the host of sages will arrange my success here."

sanskrit: brahmā svayambhūr bhagavān devāś caiva diśantu me siddhim agniś ca vāyuś ca puruhūtaś ca vajradhṛt
english: "May Brahmā the self-born, the blessed Lord, and the gods grant me success — Agni, Vāyu, and Puruhūta the wielder of the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: varuṇaḥ pāśahastaś ca somādityai tathaiva ca aśvinau ca mahātmānau marutaḥ sarva eva ca
english: "May Varuṇa with his noose, Soma and the Ādityas, the two great-souled Aśvins, and all the Maruts grant me success."

sanskrit: siddhiṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhūtānāṃ caiva yaḥ prabhuḥ dāsyanti mama ye cānye adṛṣṭāḥ pathi gocarāḥ
english: "May all beings grant me success, and he who is the lord of all beings, and whatever others, unseen, range along my path."

sanskrit: tad unnasaṃ pāṇḍuradantam avraṇaṃ śucismitaṃ padmapalāśalocanam drakṣye tad āryāvadanaṃ kadā nv ahaṃ prasannatārādhipatulyadarśanam
english: "When shall I behold that noble face — with its upturned nose, white teeth, unblemished, with a pure smile, with eyes like lotus petals, appearing like the bright full moon?"

sanskrit: kṣudreṇa pāpena nṛśaṃsakarmaṇā sudāruṇālāṃkṛtaveṣadhāriṇā balābhibhūtā abalā tapasvinī kathaṃ nu me dṛṣṭapathe 'dya sā bhavet
english: "By that wretched, sinful, cruel-acting one, wearing a most dreadful adornment and garb — overwhelmed by force, that helpless ascetic woman: when will she come within my sight today?"

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyatvā manasā cādhigamya tām avapluto mahātejāḥ prākāraṃ tasya veśmanaḥ
english: Having reflected for a moment and reaching it first in his mind, the greatly resplendent one leaped down to the enclosure wall of that mansion.

sanskrit: sa tu saṃhṛṣṭasarvāṅgaḥ prākārastho mahākapiḥ puṣpitāgrān vasantādau dadarśa vividhān drumān
english: Standing on the enclosure wall, every limb thrilled with joy, that great monkey beheld in the early spring various trees flowering at their crests.

sanskrit: sālān aśokān bhavyāṃś ca campakāṃś ca supuṣpitān uddālakān nāgavṛkṣāṃś cūtān kapimukhān api
english: Śala trees, aśoka trees, bhavya trees, beautifully blossoming campaka trees, uddālaka trees, nāga trees, mango trees, and kapimukha trees as well —

sanskrit: athāmravaṇasaṃchannāṃ latāśatasamāvṛtām jyāmukta iva nārācaḥ pupluve vṛkṣavāṭikām
english: — he leaped into that tree-garden dense with mango groves and entwined with hundreds of creepers, like an iron arrow loosed from a bowstring.

sanskrit: sa praviṣya vicitrāṃ tāṃ vihagair abhināditām rājataiḥ kāñcanaiś caiva pādapaiḥ sarvatovṛtām
english: Entering that wondrous place resounding with birds, surrounded on all sides by silver and golden trees,

sanskrit: vihagair mṛgasaṃghaiś ca vicitrāṃ citrakānanām uditādityasaṃkāśāṃ dadarśa hanumān kapiḥ
english: — vivid with birds and herds of deer, a grove of marvellous colors, blazing like the risen sun — Hanūmān the monkey beheld it.

sanskrit: vṛtāṃ nānāvidhair vṛkṣaiḥ puṣpopagaphalopagaiḥ kokilair bhṛṅgarājaiś ca mattair nityaniṣevitām
english: Surrounded by trees of every kind laden with flowers and fruit, always frequented by intoxicated kokilas and king-crows —

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanuje kale mṛgapakṣisamākule mattabarhiṇasaṃghuṣṭāṃ nānādvijagaṇāyutām
english: — in a season delightful to the human heart, teeming with deer and birds, resounding with drunken peacocks, filled with many flocks of birds —

sanskrit: mārgamāṇo varārohāṃ rājaputrīm aninditām sukhaprasuptān vihagān bodhayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: — while searching for that blameless princess of noble bearing, the monkey awakened birds sleeping in comfort.

sanskrit: utpatadbhir dvijagaṇaiḥ pakṣaiḥ sālāḥ samāhatāḥ anekavarṇā vividhā mumucuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ
english: Struck by the wings of the flocks of birds as they took flight, the śāla trees of many hues released showers of blossoms of every variety.

sanskrit: puṣpāvakīrṇaḥ śuśubhe hanumān mārutātmajaḥ aśokavanikāmadhye yathā puṣpamayo giriḥ
english: Strewn with blossoms, Hanūmān son of the Wind shone in the midst of the Aśoka grove like a mountain composed of flowers.

sanskrit: diśaḥ sarvābhidāvantaṃ vṛkṣaṣaṇḍagataṃ kapim dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni vasanta iti menire
english: Seeing the monkey moving through the thickets of trees in all directions, all living beings took him for the season of spring.

sanskrit: vṛkṣebhyaḥ patitaiḥ puṣpair avakīrṇā pṛthagvidhaiḥ rarāja vasudhā tatra pramadeva vibhūṣitā
english: Strewn with blossoms of every variety fallen from the trees, the earth there blazed like a young woman adorned.

sanskrit: tarasvinā te taravas tarasābhiprakampitāḥ kusumāni vicitrāṇi sasṛjuḥ kapinā tadā
english: Those trees, shaken with speed by that swift monkey, then shed their many-colored flowers.

sanskrit: nirdhūtapatraśikharāḥ śīrṇapuṣpaphaladrumāḥ nikṣiptavastrābharaṇā dhūrtā iva parājitāḥ
english: With their crests stripped of leaves, their flowers and fruits shed, they were like rogues stripped of their garments and ornaments in defeat.

sanskrit: hanūmatā vegavatā kampitās te nagottamāḥ puṣpaparṇaphalāny āśu mumucuḥ puṣpaśālinaḥ
english: Those finest of trees, shaken by the swift Hanūmān, quickly shed their flowers, leaves and fruits — those trees so full of blossoms.

sanskrit: vihaṃgasaṃghair hīnās te skandhamātrāśrayā drumāḥ babhūvur agamāḥ sarve māruteneva nirdhutāḥ
english: Stripped of their flocks of birds, those trees with only trunks remaining became utterly inaccessible, as if shaken by a storm-wind.

sanskrit: vidhūtakeśī yuvatir yathā mṛditavarṇikā niṣpītaśubhadantauṣṭhī nakhair dantaiś ca vikṣatā
english: Like a young woman with her hair disheveled, her cosmetics smeared, her beautiful lips and teeth drained of color, scratched by nails and teeth —

sanskrit: tathā lāṅgūlahastaiś ca caraṇābhyāṃ ca marditā babhūvāśokavanikā prabhagnavarapādapā
english: — so the Aśoka grove, trampled by tail, hands and feet, with its fine trees broken, appeared.

sanskrit: mahālatānāṃ dāmāni vyadhamat tarasā kapiḥ yathā prāvṛṣi vindhyasya meghajālāni mārutaḥ
english: The monkey swiftly scattered the garlands of great creepers as the wind scatters masses of cloud from the Vindhyas in the rainy season.

sanskrit: sa tatra maṇibhūmīś ca rājatīś ca manoramāḥ tathā kāñcanabhūmīś ca vicaran dadṛśe kapiḥ
english: Roaming there, the monkey beheld ground paved with jewels, charming grounds paved with silver, and grounds paved with gold.

sanskrit: vāpīś ca vividhākārāḥ pūrṇāḥ paramavāriṇā mahārhair maṇisopānair upapannās tataḥ sarvataḥ sarvataḥ
english: Pools of various shapes filled with the finest water, furnished here and there with stairways of precious gems —

sanskrit: muktāpravālasikatā sphaṭikāntarakuṭṭimāḥ kāñcanais tarubhiś citrais tīrajair upaśobhitāḥ
english: — their sands of pearl and coral, their floors inlaid with crystal, adorned by varied golden trees growing along their banks —

sanskrit: phullapadmotpalavanāś cakravākopakūjitāḥ natyūharutasaṃghuṣṭā haṃsasārasanāditāḥ
english: — with groves of blooming lotuses and blue water-lilies, filled with the murmur of cakravāka birds, resounding with the calls of nātyūha birds, echoing with the cries of geese and cranes —

sanskrit: dīrghābhir drumayuktābhiḥ saridbhiś ca samantataḥ amṛtopamatoyābhiḥ śivābhir upasaṃskṛtāḥ
english: — adorned all around by long streams lined with trees whose water resembled nectar, auspicious streams —

sanskrit: latāśatair avatatāḥ santānakasamāvṛtāḥ nānāgulmāvṛtavanāḥ karavīrakṛtāntarāḥ
english: — canopied by hundreds of creepers, covered with santānaka trees, their groves clothed in various shrubs, with spaces made by karavīra plants —

sanskrit: tato 'mbudharasaṃkāśaṃ pravṛddhaśikharaṃ girim vicitrakūṭaṃ kūṭaiś ca sarvataḥ parivāritam
english: — then he beheld a mountain resembling a rain-cloud, with high peaks, with varied summits, surrounded on all sides by crests —

sanskrit: śilāgṛhair avatataṃ nānāvṛkṣaiḥ samāvṛtam dadarśa kapiśārdūlo ramyaṃ jagati parvatam
english: — canopied by caves in the rock, covered with many kinds of trees: that tiger among monkeys beheld the loveliest mountain in the world.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca nagāt tasmān nadīṃ nipatitāṃ kapiḥ aṅkād iva samutpatya priyasya patitāṃ priyām
english: The monkey also beheld a river fallen from that mountain — like a beloved woman who has sprung from the lap of her beloved and fallen away.

sanskrit: jale nipatitāgraiś ca pādapair upaśobhitām vāryamāṇām iva kruddhāṃ pramadāṃ priyabandhubhiḥ
english: Adorned by trees with their tops plunged into the water, she was like an angry young woman being restrained by her dear kinsmen.

sanskrit: punar āvṛttatoyāṃ ca dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ prasannām iva kāntasya kāntāṃ punar upasthitām
english: That great monkey beheld her with water turning back again, like a beloved who, now clear-hearted, returns to her beloved once more.

sanskrit: tasyādūrāt sa padminyo nānādvijagaṇāyutāḥ dadarśa kapiśārdūlo hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Not far from her, that tiger among monkeys, Hanūmān son of the Wind, beheld lotus ponds filled with many flocks of birds.

sanskrit: kṛtrimāṃ dīrghikāṃ cāpi pūrṇāṃ śītena vāriṇā maṇipravarasopānāṃ muktāsikataśobhitām
english: He also beheld an artificial pool filled with cool water, its stairways of finest gems, adorned with sands of pearl.

sanskrit: vividhair mṛgasaṃghaiś ca vicitrāṃ citrakānanām prāsādaiḥ sumahadbhiś ca nirmitair viśvakarmaṇā kānanaiḥ kṛtrimaiś cāpi sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtām
english: Vivid with various herds of deer, with wonderful colorful groves, adorned all around by grand palaces built by Viśvakarman and by artificial woodlands —

sanskrit: ye ke cit pādapās tatra puṣpopagaphalopagāḥ sacchatrāḥ savitardīkāḥ sarve sauvarṇavedikāḥ
english: — whatever trees were there bearing flowers and fruit, all were well-furnished with canopies and parasols, all with golden platforms.

sanskrit: latāpratānair bahubhiḥ parṇaiś ca bahubhir vṛtām kāñcanīṃ śiṃśupām ekāṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: Entwined with many spreading creepers and covered with many leaves, that great monkey beheld a single golden śiṃśupā tree.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad bhūmibhāgāṃś ca gartaprasravaṇāni ca suvarṇavṛkṣān aparān dadarśa śikhisaṃnibhān
english: He saw stretches of ground and gullies with springs; he saw other golden trees resembling peacocks.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ drumāṇāṃ prabhayā meror iva mahākapiḥ amanyata tadā vīraḥ kāñcano 'smīti vānaraḥ
english: By the radiance of those trees, that heroic monkey, great among monkeys, then imagined, as if by the light of Meru, that he himself had become golden.

sanskrit: tāṃ kāñcanais tarugaṇair mārutena ca vījitām kiṅkiṇīśatanirghoṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayam āgamat
english: Seeing that grove fanned by the breeze among its company of golden trees, resounding with hundreds of tinkling bells, he was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: supuṣpitāgrāṃ rucirāṃ taruṇāṅkurapallavām tām āruhya mahāvegaḥ śiṃśapāṃ parṇasaṃvṛtām
english: The greatly swift one climbed that śiṃśupā tree — beautiful with fully flowered crest, with tender shoots and sprouts, covered with foliage —

sanskrit: ito drakṣyāmi vaidehīṃ rāma darśanalālasām itaś cetaś ca duḥkhārtāṃ saṃpatantīṃ yadṛcchayā
english: — thinking: "From here I shall see Vaidehī, longing to behold Rāma, wandering here and there, tormented by grief, coming about by chance."

sanskrit: aśokavanikā ceyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ ramyā durātmanaḥ campakaiś candanaiś cāpi bakulaiś ca vibhūṣitā
english: "And this Aśoka grove of the evil-souled one is truly lovely, adorned with campaka, sandalwood and bakula trees."

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca nalinī ramyā dvijasaṃghaniṣevitā imāṃ sā rāmamahiṣī nūnam eṣyati jānakī
english: "And this charming lotus pool, frequented by flocks of birds — Jānakī, the great queen of Rāma, will surely come to this."

sanskrit: sā rāma rāmamahiṣī rāghavasya priyā sadā vanasaṃcārakuśalā nūnam eṣyati jānakī
english: "She — Rāma's great queen, always dear to Rāghava, well-versed in roaming through forests — Jānakī will surely come here."

sanskrit: atha vā mṛgaśāvākṣī vanasyāsya vicakṣaṇā vanam eṣyati sā ceha rāmacintānukarśitā
english: "Or that woman with eyes like a young deer's, knowing this forest well, she who is worn thin by thoughts of Rāma, will come to this grove."

sanskrit: rāmaśokābhisaṃtaptā sā devī vāmalocanā vanavāsaratā nityam eṣyate vanacāriṇī
english: "That goddess of lovely eyes, ever delighting in forest-dwelling, she who ever roams the forest — scorched by grief for Rāma, she will come here."

sanskrit: vanecarāṇāṃ satataṃ nūnaṃ spṛhayate purā rāmasya dayitā bhāryā janakasya sutā satī
english: "Formerly she who is the beloved wife of Rāma, the faithful daughter of Janaka, always yearned for those who roam in the forest."

sanskrit: saṃdhyākālamanāḥ śyāmā dhruvam eṣyati jānakī nadīṃ cemāṃ śivajalāṃ saṃdhyārthe varavarṇinī
english: "At the time of twilight, dark-complexioned Jānakī, of noble hue, will certainly come to this auspicious river for the evening rite."

sanskrit: tasyāś cāpy anurūpeyam aśokavanikā śubhā śubhā yā pārthivendrasya patnī rāmasya saṃmitā
english: "And this auspicious Aśoka grove befits her — she who is the consort of the lord of the earth's sons and the match of Rāma."

sanskrit: yadi jivati sā devī tārādhipanibhānanā āgamiṣyati sāvaśyam imāṃ śivajalāṃ nadīm
english: "If that goddess lives — she whose face resembles the lord of the stars — she will certainly come to this auspicious river."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu matvā hanumān mahātmā pratīkṣamāṇo manujendrapatnīm avekṣamāṇaś ca dadarśa sarvaṃ supuṣpite parṇaghane nilīnaḥ
english: Thus reasoning, the great-souled Hanūmān, waiting and watching for the wife of the lord of men, concealed in the dense foliage of the fully blossoming tree, surveyed everything.
